title: Anacephalaeosis [Sp.]
author: Epiphanius
source: Translated by Claude from tlg2021.tlg003.1st1K-grc1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς κατὰ Μένανδρον ὑπὸ ἀγγέλων τὸν κόσμον γεγενῆσθαι ἔφασκεν, μόνων δὲ ἑπτά, παρὰ τὴν τοῦ ἄνω πατρὸς γνωμην.
passages.english: He too, following Menander, used to say that the world had come into being through angels, but only seven, contrary to the will of the Father above.
passages.notes: The subject is unnamed in the passage; in heresiological catalogues this description usually belongs to Saturnilus (Satornilus). "γνωμην" read as γνώμην (accent missing). "Following Menander" (κατὰ Μένανδρον) could also be taken as "like Menander".

passages.original: λݲγݲ. Πτολεμαῖοι, μαθηταὶ ὄντες καὶ αὐτοὶ Οὐαλεντίνου, οἷς συνάπτεται ἡ Φλώρα. τὰ αὐτὰ δὲ περὶ τῶν συζυγιῶν καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγουσι καθάπερ Οὐαλεντῖνος καὶ Σεκουνδιανοί· κατά τι δὲ καὶ οὗτοι διαφέρονται.
passages.english: 33. Ptolemaeans, who are themselves also disciples of Valentinus; with them Flora is associated. They too say the same things about the syzygies [paired emanations] as Valentinus and the Secundians, but in some respect these also differ.
passages.notes: The numeral λγ (33) carries combining marks from the edition. 'Flora' is presumably the addressee of Ptolemy's Letter to Flora.

passages.original: μݲγ.ݲ. Λουκιανισταί. Λουκιανός τις ἀρχαῖος, οὐχ ὁ νῦν έν χρόνοις Κωνσταντίνου γενόμενος, πάντα κατὰ Μαρκίωνα ἐδογμάτισεν, ἕτερα δὲ παρὰ τὸν Μαρκίωνα καὶ αὐτὸς δῆθεν περισσοτέρως δογματίζει.
passages.english: 43. Lucianists. A certain Lucian of old, not the one who lived recently in the times of Constantine, taught everything in accordance with Marcion, but he himself also, supposedly, teaches other things beyond Marcion, more extensively.
passages.notes: The numeral μγ (43) carries combining marks from the edition. The numbering jumps from 33 to 43 between these two units, so the units are not consecutive. 'έν' is read as ἐν. 'Beyond Marcion' could also mean 'contrary to Marcion' (παρά).
